posts.body:
This is probably more deserving of a dedicated topic, but it's just that for my game, I'm just not satisfied with existing plugin solutions.
A piece of missing info some people may have here on RMW is that also I have a PM from Turan that further elaborates, but since both seem sort of connected, I feel like I should just address the point as a whole.
So his PM was basically wondering why I feel like I should throw money at custom plugins, rather than using the existing publicly released plugins.
First of all; there is nothing wrong with anyone who uses them, this doesn't come from a place of superiority "because I can."
It's mostly just that, many plugins just don't seem to meet my vision. It often feels like things have to be compromised on.
Many plugins either lack enough customization, lack adequate documentation, lack notetags and plugin commands that I would need, always requiring me to find some sort of duct tape solution - never mind the fact that not all plugins are tested very well and often have oversights, crashes, or incompatibilities.
I don't
expect
every plugin to have all of the features I want because they are offered for free or at the very least developed by a hobbyist programmer. But it unfortately means that the plugins just fail to meet my vision.
Getting support for plugins is also tough; like Yanfly is pretty easy because it's so ubiquitous, but beyond that it gets tough to find people to help with specific plugins or patch things. Only some popular names stick out; SRD, Galv, Hime, and Eli. Even then, it took me some 4 - 6 months (I don't remember) to get the solution to a problem I had with galv's layer graphics.
The number of problems that arise from introducing a new plugin to my project often just causes a lot of headaches; like, sure the plugin for what I want to do already exists, but then it feels like I often have to spend the next week just getting the thing to behave properly before I can even make the mechanic I want. Here's just a few examples of what I am talking about:
SRD has mindless copy-paste errors in some of his plugins, and poor documentation that sent me on a wild goose chase.
Aries charges money for their plugins but has a typo in the code that crashes the plugin if a specific function is used.
Not so long ago Arthran was having to patch a memory leak in Olivia's plugin. Not one I use, but again just goes to show, if you haven't read (and understood) the actual code of the plugin, you have no idea what you are introducing into your game.
The Pixi Filter's documentation is ultra dog-water that I spent like 3 days just trying to determine wtf the dev was talking about.
The number of weird things I've run into using Yanfly plugins; a simple example that comes to mind is, funnily enough, Keyboard config. Maybe it's just personal bias, but seems like a weird oversight that he has basically preset keyboard layouts (arrows or WASD) but there is no plugin command to set what the default preset layout is.
Documentation on creating options in Yanfly options core is a/s.
Some more reliable plugin devs have minor annoyances that crop up, though admittedly these could just be because my plugin load is quite large.
Eli's escape codes everywhere plugin ruins the formatting of a lot of text in the game (you can see in my game where the word RANK overlaps Fidel's name in the victory aftermath screen) and the fix for this is located in a completely separate plugin that may be incompatible with one of my other plugins.
Hime's stuff is mostly reliable but just better hope nothing does go wrong because she's MIA, like many, many other devs.
Galv at least still pops in from time to time to offer support for his plugins.
I could probably go all day listing off all of these frustrations, but really my point is:
You know what I really don't enjoy doing? Troubleshooting someone else's work. I just want to focus on making my game.
All these points addressed above are the technical problems with using existing plugin solutions, this don't even address the resulting "cookie-cutter" nature that tends to come out of them.
By having custom plugins made it means:
I can spend more time focusing on making my game.
The result will meet my vision both visually and technically.
To me, this is worth the cost.
That doesn't mean I'm saying "NO!" to all plugins. There are some plugins that I can still use. Especially utility plugins that don't add new mechanics but basically just expand on what the editor can do are very valuable (such as event spawners I would consider utility)
What I am saying is that there are many aspects of my game that I feel it would be better to have something custom made for it.
And I'm running out of time to type out this rant, lol. So let's leave it at that.
We can start a topic discussing it if you want.
